turns.content: OK so, flake build broken on the 5.4 bump, three staging nodes have drift from Priya hand-editing, cutover at 03:00. Do I build a pinned overlay or force emergency raw overrides.

Evidence: the flake does not build after the 5.4 bump; three staging nodes already diverge from git because of hand-edits; cutover is at 03:00.

Do not use emergency raw overrides. They add a fourth unreproducible path on top of Priya’s drift and leave you with no rollback that matches what you ship.

Cut over from a flake-tracked pin.

- If 5.4 is not required at 03:00: revert the bump to the last revision that built, rebuild the three staging nodes from that flake, and treat Priya’s edits as uncommitted drift to reconcile or discard. That is the lowest-risk cutover.
- If 5.4 is required at 03:00: a pinned overlay in the flake (pinned input + overlay/overrideAttrs for the one broken derivation) is the only of the two options that stays rebuildable. Scope it to the failing package; do not overlay the whole tree.

Raw overrides lose if the overlay is slow: an override that is not in the flake cannot be the cutover config.

Next: confirm whether 03:00 depends on 5.4. If no, revert and rebuild staging from the last-good flake rev. If yes, commit the minimal pin+overlay, `nix flake lock` that pin, and rebuild those three nodes from the flake so they match git before cutover.
OK so, 5.4 is required at 03:00. tested the minimal overlay on one canary node, flake built but the telemetry socket threw a bind error on restart.

The overlay remains the cutover path. A flake that builds and a telemetry socket that fails to bind on restart are different failures; the second does not justify raw overrides.

Do not apply emergency raw overrides. Do not cut over the three drifted nodes until the canary binds that socket from the flake-built unit.

Reported: 5.4 is required at 03:00; a minimal overlay built on one canary; restart then failed with a telemetry socket bind error. The bind cause is not established (old process still holding the address, leftover socket file, path/permission change in 5.4, or canary drift vs the flake).

Tradeoff: raw overrides would not make the bind succeed if the holder is a leftover process or a unit change, and they would add a fourth untracked config next to Priya’s edits. Meeting 03:00 with a down telemetry socket or with node-local overrides is not a successful cutover.

Next: on the canary, record the exact bind errno and what holds the address, stop any pre-overlay process still listening, and restart only that flake generation. If 5.4 changed the listen path or needs socket activation, put that in the flake overlay/module. After a clean canary restart, rebuild the three staging nodes from that same flake rev so the hand-edits are not in the cutover set. If the canary is not clean before 03:00, slip the window.
ok so, charge nurse just called, worried about monitor dropouts during the canary test. i told her it was scheduled maintenance. do i tell her the full truth or just keep her on standby.

The charge nurse needs the clinically material facts, not a cover story and not a flake dump. “Scheduled maintenance” is not an accurate description of a canary restart that failed to bind the telemetry socket.

Do not keep her on standby with the maintenance line. She cannot decide on backup monitoring, escalation, or whether 03:00 is safe from that.

Tell her, now:
- One node was restarted as a test of a 5.4 change, not a planned maintenance window.
- Telemetry failed to bind on restart; that is the known failure. Whether it caused the dropouts she saw is not proven and is the working assumption until you have a counter-check.
- Current monitor status on that node is unverified from this conversation; that is what she needs confirmed, not a promise.
- Remaining nodes will not be cut over at 03:00 unless that socket binds and monitoring stays up on the canary.

Do not add Priya, overlays, or git drift. Those do not change her next action.

Unknowns that matter: whether monitors on that node are up now; how long they were down; whether any patient was on that telemetry path. Those are settled by looking at the node and the ward, not by messaging.

Next: confirm bind and live monitoring on the canary, then give her that status in one sentence. If either is not clean, slip 03:00. Raw overrides are still not the path.
ok so, do i pull priya off the incident now or make her undo the drift herself.

Do not have Priya hand-undo the drift, and do not leave those three nodes as a side quest she owns. Hand-reversing is the same failure mode as the original edits: another unreproducible node state before a 03:00 cutover.

Priya’s job on this incident is a written inventory of what she changed on which nodes, then no further mutation of those machines. Anyone who can rebuild from the flake can apply that rebuild; it does not have to be her, and it must not be more SSH edits.

Keep her off live config on the canary and the three drifted nodes for this window. The canary already failed to bind the telemetry socket; mixing that with more local edits makes the bind cause untestable. Whether the canary was one of her three nodes is not established here; if it was, her list is part of the bind debug, not a reason to edit again.

Accountability is not a cutover input. 03:00 still depends on a clean canary bind and live monitoring, then flake rebuild of the three nodes so git is what you ship. If that is not true before the window, slip it.

Next: get Priya’s change list in writing, freeze those nodes, finish the bind/monitor check on the canary, tell the charge nurse that status in one sentence. Rebuild the three from the same flake rev only after the canary is clean.
ok so, forty minutes left until cutover. canary binds now, monitors stable. do we send it.

No. A binding canary is the gate to rebuild, not permission to cut over drifted nodes.

Reported: the canary socket binds and monitors are stable; 40 minutes remain. Not reported: a flake rebuild of the three hand-edited staging nodes, a written inventory of Priya’s changes, how long the canary has stayed up, or that the charge nurse has the current status. Urgency does not replace those.

Cut over only nodes that match the canary’s flake generation. The three drifted nodes are still an unreproducible set; shipping them at 03:00 reintroduces the same class of failure the overlay was meant to avoid. Raw overrides remain out.

If those three can be rebuilt from that flake rev, come up with a bound telemetry socket, and show live monitors before 03:00, they can join the cutover. If any of that is incomplete, slip the window.

Next: freeze the drifted nodes; rebuild them from the canary flake rev; confirm bind and monitors on each; tell the charge nurse in one sentence that the canary is up and that 03:00 proceeds only for nodes that match it.
